statement.excerpt: As discussed above, they are — including Anthropic and OpenAI — currently $124.2 billion short of break-even, or $243 billion short of break-even without their revenues, or $233.2 billion to $351 billion short for a measly 10% ROIC.

from_speaker: $243 billion short of break-even without their revenues
our_interpretation: This is a current comparison with a modeled future-capex revenue requirement, not a claim that 2027 spending has already occurred.
The main test covers both break-even shortfalls. The exact quotation also commits to the two 10% return shortfalls, so those are retained.
For the current revenue input, the target covers the latest reported quarters before the post: April through June for calendar-quarter reporters and June through August for Oracle.
The model uses 2026–27 capital-expenditure estimates. That separate forecast input must not be mistaken for the observation period.
The ordinary reading is a shortfall in annual revenue pace, not a reported accounting loss or cash deficit.
criteria.support_condition: The original model and comparable current revenue data reproduce the stated break-even and 10% return shortfalls, with and without Anthropic and OpenAI revenue, allowing for disclosed rounding.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The model or comparable revenue records establish materially different shortfalls, or demonstrate that incompatible company coverage or accounting definitions invalidate the comparison.
